justification: Both surfaces carry schematic low-relief anthropomorphic imagery with raised or bent arms, and A includes a circular disc motif while B's figures make similar gestural forms, but this is about as generic as figural carving gets. A is a single large frontal standing figure with abstract emblems (disc, bands, headdress-like top) covering a monolithic body, whereas B shows a horizontal frieze of several small crouching/seated figures interacting in a narrative row — a wholly different compositional scheme and figure type.
